title: Pride, Prejudice and Judgement
text:
In Pride and Prejudice, Jane Austen follows Elizabeth Bennet, the second of five daughters in a family whose estate is entailed to a male cousin. Her mother is anxious to see her daughters married well, and the arrival of wealthy bachelors in the neighbourhood sets the plot in motion. Austen uses wit and irony to expose the social pressures placed upon women of limited means. Her irony gives the novel much of its enduring charm.

Elizabeth's first impression of Mr Darcy is unfavourable, and she is quick to judge him proud and disdainful. Her prejudice is matched by his own, as he initially considers her family beneath his notice. Austen gradually reveals that both characters must correct their misjudgements before any real understanding can develop. The eventual reconciliation therefore depends less on fortune than on self-knowledge.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what is the situation of the Bennet family's estate?
options: It is sold to pay the family's debts
It is entailed to a male cousin
It is given to the eldest daughter
It is shared equally among the five daughters

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what is Elizabeth's first impression of Mr Darcy?
options: Unfavourable, seeing him as proud and disdainful

questions.text: What does the passage imply about the marriage prospects of women like Elizabeth?
options: They have complete freedom to choose their own fortunes
They are shaped by economic pressure
They are unaffected by their family's wealth

questions.text: What is implied about the reconciliation between Elizabeth and Darcy?
options: It depends mainly on the size of Darcy's fortune
It happens by chance without any change in character
It is impossible because of their social rank
It requires both characters to recognise their own faults

vocabulary.definition: legally bound to pass on to a specific person, usually a male heir
a way of expressing meaning in which the intended sense is the opposite of what is said
an opinion formed in advance without enough knowledge or thought
showing a feeling that someone or something is unworthy of respect

paragraph_translations: Jane Austen'ın Pride and Prejudice adlı romanında okur, beş kızdan ikincisi olan Elizabeth Bennet'i takip eder; ailelerinin malikânesi bir erkek kuzene miras kalmıştır. Annesi kızlarının iyi evlenmesini çok istemekte, komşulukta beliren zengin bekârlar ise olayları harekete geçirmektedir. Austen, sınırlı imkânlara sahip kadınların üzerindeki toplumsal baskıyı açığa çıkarmak için zekâ ve ironiyi kullanır. Yazarın ironisi romanın kalıcı cazibesinin büyük bölümünü oluşturur.

Elizabeth'in Mr Darcy hakkındaki ilk izlenimi olumsuzdur; onu gururlu ve küçümseyici biri olarak görmekte gecikmez. Bu önyargıya, Darcy'nin de kendi önyargısıyla karşılık verdiği görülür, çünkü başlangıçta Elizabeth'in ailesini dikkate değmez bulur. Austen, gerçek bir anlayışın gelişebilmesi için iki karakterin de yanlış yargılarını düzeltmek zorunda olduğunu yavaş yavaş ortaya koyar. Sonunda gerçekleşen barışma, bu nedenle servete değil, öz farkındalığa bağlıdır.
